quick_notes.title: BODMAS Rule
quick_notes.detail: Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. The absolute order of operations.
quick_notes.explanation: The BODMAS rule is a set of instructions that tells you the correct order to do math operations when you see a problem with different symbols like brackets, plus, minus, times, and divide. BODMAS stands for Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. The word "Bracket" means any part of the problem that is inside parentheses ( ), curly braces { }, or square brackets [ ]; you must solve what is inside those brackets first. The word "Of" means you should handle any "of" statement, like "half of 10" or "2/3 of 9", which is actually a multiplication you do right after the brackets. After brackets and "of", you do all Division and Multiplication from left to right, and then you do all Addition and Subtraction from left to right. For example, in the problem 2 + 3 x 4, you do the multiplication 3 x 4 = 12 first, then add 2 to get 14; if you did the addition first you would get a wrong answer of 20.

quick_notes.title: Percentage Table
quick_notes.explanation: A percentage is a way to show a number as a part of 100. For example, 50 percent (50%) means 50 out of 100, which is the same as the fraction one-half. To help you calculate quickly, memorize these common fractions and their equal percentages: one-half is 50%, one-third is about 33.3%, one-fourth is 25%, one-fifth is 20%, one-sixth is about 16.6%, and one-eighth is 12.5%. These are called equivalent values because the fraction and the percentage represent the same amount. You can use these shortcuts whenever you need to find a percentage of a number, like figuring out what 25% of 200 is by remembering that one-fourth of 200 is 50.

quick_notes.title: Ratio & Proportion
quick_notes.detail: A:B and B:C -> A:B:C calculation. Third/Fourth Proportional. Mean Proportional : sqrt(ab).
quick_notes.explanation: A ratio compares two numbers, like 2:3 means for every 2 of one thing there are 3 of another. A proportion states that two ratios are equal, such as 2:3 = 4:6. If you have two ratios A:B and B:C, you can find the combined ratio A:B:C by making the B terms the same using their least common multiple. quick_notes.title: Simplification Tricks
quick_notes.detail: Approximation. Using unit digits. Division by 9/11 rules.
quick_notes.explanation: Simplification tricks are methods to make math calculations faster and easier. Approximation means rounding numbers to the nearest ten, hundred, or thousand so you can quickly estimate an answer instead of finding the exact value. Using unit digits means looking only at the last digit of a number to determine properties like whether a product ends in a certain digit, which can help you check answers or solve problems without doing the full multiplication. The division by 9 rule says that if you add all the digits of a number and the sum is divisible by 9, then the original number is also divisible by 9. The division by 11 rule says that if you find the alternating sum of the digits (starting from the leftmost digit, subtract the next, add the next, and so on) and that result is 0 or a multiple of 11, then the original number is divisible by 11. These tricks help you solve problems faster and with less calculation.

quick_notes.title: Squares (1-30)
quick_notes.explanation: A square is the result of multiplying a number by itself. For example, 15 squared means 15 times 15, which equals 225. You should remember these specific squares: 11 squared is 121, 13 squared is 169, 15 squared is 225, 17 squared is 289, 19 squared is 361, and 25 squared is 625.
